engine: None of its own. The agent writes a .ts script and runs it in the user's shell with tsx or node, as a normal OS process with the user's files, network, environment and credentials. The package is a client library and CLI for calling MCP servers.
how_run: Each probe is a .ts file run as a fresh `tsx <file>` process (the runner the README's example uses, README.md:173); the lookup tool is a local stdio MCP server reached through the package's exported StdioMcpClient. The documented mcp.<server> proxy was not used because its name resolution reads the macOS Keychain (see source_notes).

defaults.time: None. The package sets no timeout on scripts or on tool calls (no timeout or AbortSignal in src/).
defaults.memory: None from the project; Node's default heap only.
defaults.output: None from the project. The script's stdout goes to whatever ran it.
defaults.hardened: null: the project exposes no stricter option. It ships no runner, so there is nothing to configure; isolation would have to come from the user's agent or OS.

source_notes.finding: There is none, by design. The README's own comparison table lists 'Where the code runs: your shell' and says 'No sandbox to deploy'. The package never executes model code; the coding agent writes a script and runs it with tsx in its Bash tool. Code mode here means 'no model between calls', not 'contained code'.

The library's purpose is to hand scripts the user's MCP credentials: McpClient.fromClaudeCode reads the OAuth token from the macOS Keychain item 'Claude Code-credentials' with `security find-generic-password -s ... -w`, plus ~/.claude/.credentials.json. Even a stdio server lookup through mcp.<name> or openSession runs resolveName -> listServers -> listCredentials, which reads the whole Keychain blob. Credentials therefore live inside the process that runs model-written code. SECURITY.md says any process spawned from a Claude Code session can read every MCP token without a prompt.

Reads MCP server definitions from ~/.claude.json, <cwd>/.mcp.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, Windsurf, VS Code settings and Gemini settings, expanding ${VAR} from the environment. HOME is honoured, so config can be redirected, but the Keychain read cannot.

A runtime Proxy: mcp.<server>.<method>(args) opens a session lazily and maps camelCase back to the wire tool name against the live tools/list. `agent-codemode types` generates a TS module per server (one Args interface per tool, JSDoc clipped) that merges into the McpServers interface for compile-time checks.

No in-prompt catalog and no search tool: the agent runs `agent-codemode servers`, `tools <server>` or `types --all` in its shell and reads files. Scales with the agent's own file reading, not a schema dump.

Direct MCP from the script process: Streamable HTTP via fetch for remote servers, newline-delimited JSON-RPC over a spawned child's stdin/stdout for stdio servers. Stdio servers are spawned with {...process.env, ...cfg.env}, so they inherit the script's whole environment.

None of these are handled by the project: output is the script's stdout, errors are Node's uncaught-exception print and exit code, there are no time, memory, output or call limits, and each run is a new process. CLI exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 tool isError.
MIT; version 0.1.1; last commit 2026-08-19 (docs). Small (about 1,550 lines of TS), tests are one smoke script with an echo server.

surprises: Not a sandboxed code mode at all: the shipped skill tells the agent to write scripts that run in the user's shell with the user's tokens. It meets the narrow definition (code calls tools, only output returns to the model) with no isolation, so it cannot pass G1, G2 or G3.
Resolving any server name through mcp.<name>, openSession or the CLI reads the entire Claude Code Keychain blob (every MCP token), even when the target is a local stdio server that needs no token.

tsx runs the script in a grandchild process. Killing the tsx process on a timeout left the spinning P6 script orphaned at 100% CPU until the harness killed it by PID; an agent's Bash timeout that kills only its direct child would leave the same orphan.
The README's '290x less into context, 99.66% saved' figure is one prompt against the author's live Linear workspace; it is not reproducible from the repo (no benchmark script ships).
